question_for_user: The DEV split cannot supply the DEV250 composition natively. The exact quotas are 50 no-op, 110 finish_block, 28 pipe_rewrite, 24 format, 23 rename, 11 roxygen and 4 na_rm (250 cases, 200 edits). Under the 3-cases-per-group cap the native split yields at most 36 finish_block cases (12 groups), no new no-ops (8 native rows, all already in DEV75) and zero pipe/format/rename/na_rm rows (79 wanted). Only roxygen (127 groups) is plentiful. May I try source-derived construction over the dev_group parent sources, using the constructors TRAIN and DAT-07 used (finish_block_v5_prefix windows for finish_block, DAT-07's derived already-applied-state no-ops, and DAT-07's rename/pipe/format/na_rm companions), keeping these quotas and the 3-per-group cap? Recommended: yes, but only if a feasibility check passes first. Before building any targets, I would run the constructors in dry-run mode over the eligible pool (dev_group groups not used by DEV75 and not excluded by the CPT-overlap check) and count constructible groups per family. The check passes if each family meets its minimum group count (finish_block 37, no_op 17, pipe 10, format 8, rename 8, roxygen 4, na_rm 2) with at least 84 distinct groups overall. Passing keeps DEV250 TRAIN-like and group-disjoint, and it avoids every DAT-07-final-* file. If the check fails, I will stop and report the per-family supply. The fallbacks are then (a) a smaller panel at the same mix, (b) lower quotas for the short families, with the gap recorded, or (c) a looser cap for finish_block only, which lets a few packages dominate the finish_block score. A natively-sourced panel (about 55% roxygen, no propagation families) remains the last resort.
